Restored page, audited against extension@4.1.15 and wxt@0.21.4. Verified by running the CLI: browser-prefixed keys filtered at compile time (built one manifest for chrome and firefox, the firefox: key appears only in dist/firefox), `extension dev <github-url>` really does dev a remote sample (fetched extension-js/examples and reached ready), Rspack is the bundler (@rspack/core 2.2.3 in extension-develop), and dist/chrome plus dist/firefox with .zip archives come out of one `build --browser=chrome,firefox --zip`. Verified against the WXT package rather than memory: the CLI surface (cac commands `[root]` dev server, `build`, `zip`, `prepare`, all taking -b), MV2 via --mv2 and manifestVersion 2, the .output/${browser}-mv${manifestVersion} outDir template, Vite as the builder with peer range ^6.3.4 || ^7.0.0 || ^8.0.0-0, auto-imports through unimport, and llms.txt (https://wxt.dev/llms.txt returns 200). Four findings. First, the WXT `browser.*` polyfill claim is outdated and it drives the recommendation in three places (the TL;DR card, the At a glance row, and the When to choose WXT list): in wxt 0.21.4 `wxt/browser` re-exports @wxt-dev/browser 0.2.9, whose whole body is `globalThis.browser?.runtime?.id ? globalThis.browser : globalThis.chrome`, a native alias and not a polyfill, and webextension-polyfill appears nowhere in the wxt dist. The polyfill is now opt-in through the separate @wxt-dev/webextension-polyfill package. Second, the Templates row credits WXT with Preact, but the templates/ directory of wxt-dev/wxt holds exactly react, solid, svelte, vanilla and vue. Third, the same row credits Extension.js with WebAssembly, but `extension create --help` on 4.1.15 prints all 59 catalog names and none of them is a WebAssembly template (docs/getting-started/templates.mdx carries the same stale word in its description, outside this batch). Fourth, the Browser targets row lists Safari for WXT as community and omits it for Extension.js, which inverts the real position: safari is a first-class --browser value on 4.1.15 with its own flag group. Fixed 2026-09-09, all four findings. The outdated auto-polyfill claim was rewritten in all three places it drove the recommendation, and a new paragraph in Cross-browser strategy states the real mechanism with the version named: the card at the top and the When to choose WXT list now say `browser` is auto-imported and resolves to the native `browser` object or to `chrome`, and the At a glance row reads `browser` aliased to `chrome`, real polyfill opt-in through `@wxt-dev/webextension-polyfill`. Re-verified from the published tarballs rather than memory: the entire body of @wxt-dev/browser 0.2.9 is one export, `globalThis.browser?.runtime?.id ? globalThis.browser : globalThis.chrome`, `wxt/browser` re-exports it, a grep for webextension-polyfill matches no file in the wxt 0.21.4 package, dist/core/resolve-config.mjs registers `browser` from `wxt/browser` as an unimport preset, and @wxt-dev/webextension-polyfill 1.0.0 exists on the registry as the separate opt-in module. The Templates row lost WebAssembly on the Extension.js side, because `extension create --help` on 4.1.15 prints all 59 catalog names and none of them is a WebAssembly template, and lost Preact on the WXT side, because the templates listing endpoint the wxt CLI itself calls, https://api.github.com/repos/wxt-dev/wxt/contents/templates, returns exactly react, solid, svelte, vanilla and vue. The Browser targets row now gives Extension.js `Safari (macOS, through Xcode)`, matching `dev --help`, and gives WXT `Safari (build only, no browser launch)`, which is what wxt 0.21.4 ships: dist/core/resolve-config.mjs routes a `safari` browser to createSafariRunner, and that runner's openBrowser only warns that web-ext cannot drive Safari and that the output has to be loaded by hand. The unverifiable `community` wording is gone. One prose semicolon was also removed. No findings remain.

Restored page, migration walked with extension@4.1.15 on a hand-built project shaped like the page's own step 2 (manifest.json with action.default_popup, background.service_worker pointing at a .ts entry, one content_scripts entry, and firefox:browser_specific_settings). Verified by running: .ts and .tsx paths in the manifest and in an HTML script tag compile at build time, step 6 emits dist/chrome and dist/firefox with browser-correct manifests plus migratecheck-1.0.0.zip in each, the firefox build rewrites background.service_worker to background.scripts, and step 7 runs on both targets. The web_accessible_resources gotcha and the manifest-relative path advice both hold for `extension build`. Three findings. First, step 7 says to pass --polyfill when your code calls `chrome.*` so the same source runs on Firefox, which is backwards twice over: the polyfill supplies `browser.*` on Chromium targets, and Firefox already supports `chrome.*` natively. Observed directly, `build --browser=chrome` produced a 7,475 byte content script and `build --browser=chrome --polyfill` produced a 17,032 byte one containing webextension-polyfill. The site's own docs/features/cross-browser-compatibility.mdx states the correct rule. The same sentence also tells the reader to add a flag that `extension dev` already applies: `dev --help` says the default is true, and a plain `extension dev` emitted a content script containing webextension-polyfill. Second, the Common gotchas claim that Extension.js auto-sets `type: "module"` when the background entry uses ESM syntax did not reproduce. A background entry with a top-level import compiled to a classic IIFE and the emitted manifest carried no type key at all, while a source manifest that declares type module keeps it. Lane B record b05 reached the same conclusion independently on docs/concepts/manifest-v3.mdx. Third, the hashed-asset gotcha says Extension.js uses stable paths under dist/<browser>, which is true for build but not for dev: `extension dev` emitted content_scripts/content-0.29191618.js, and docs/features/reload-and-hmr.mdx documents that dev appends a build hash and only production builds use clean names. Fixed 2026-09-09, all three findings. Step 7 now states the real rule: `chrome.*` code runs on Firefox as written because Firefox supports that namespace natively, `--polyfill` supplies `browser.*` on Chromium targets instead, `extension dev` applies it by default and `extension build` leaves it off. Re-measured on 4.1.15 with a scratch project. With a content script that reads `browser.runtime`, `build --browser=chrome` emitted 7,436 bytes with no webextension-polyfill and `build --browser=chrome --polyfill` emitted 16,997 bytes containing it. With a `chrome.*`-only content script the two builds were byte-identical, which is the polyfill being pruned when nothing reaches it. A plain `extension dev --browser=chrome --no-browser` emitted a content script containing webextension-polyfill, which confirms the dev default that `dev --help` states. The service-worker gotcha now says Extension.js bundles the background entry so `import` needs no manifest change, that Extension.js does not add `type: "module"` for you, and that a key you declare yourself survives the build. Both halves reproduced here: a background entry with a top-level import compiled to a classic IIFE and the emitted manifest carried no type key, and after adding `"type": "module"` to the source manifest the emitted manifest kept it. The hashed-path gotcha now separates production from dev, cites the dev filename observed here, `content_scripts/content-0.813e908a.js`, and links Reload and HMR. Two prose semicolons were removed. The docs error is closed, and the underlying behaviour that b05 and this record both found is being reported to the maintainer as a possible product defect rather than only a docs defect, because two pages carried the same false claim.

Restored page, audited against extension@4.1.15 and plasmo@0.90.5. Verified by running the Extension.js half: the convention-to-manifest table entries build (action.default_popup, background.service_worker on a .ts entry, content_scripts), the HTML popup shape with a .tsx script tag compiles, step 5 emits dist/chrome and dist/firefox with .zip archives, and the EXTENSION_PUBLIC_ rename works (a .env with EXTENSION_PUBLIC_GREETING=world was inlined into the built popup as the literal `hello world`). Verified against the shipped plasmo bundle rather than memory: @parcel/core 2.9.3 confirms the Parcel base, PLASMO_PUBLIC_ is the real prefix, --target defaults to chrome-mv3 and is split on the dash into browser and manifest version, which is what makes `--target=firefox-mv2` a valid form, PlasmoCSConfig is exported from its type declarations, `~` is the project-root alias, and the sharp dependency plus the assets/icon16.plasmo.png through icon128.plasmo.png names back the auto-generated-icons gotcha. The claim that release cadence has slowed checks out: the npm registry shows 377 releases with the newest, 0.90.5, published 2025-05-17, and its @parcel/core pin of 2.9.3 sits far behind the current 2.16.4. @plasmohq/storage 1.15.0 and @plasmohq/messaging 0.7.2 both still exist. Two findings. First, the Changes list maps `plasmo package` onto `extension build --zip`, but plasmo 0.90.5 has no package command: its help block lists init, dev and build only, and zipping is `build --zip`. Second, step 6 carries the same reversed polyfill sentence as from-crxjs, telling readers with `chrome.*` code to pass --polyfill for Firefox. The polyfill supplies `browser.*` on Chromium targets (a chrome build grew from 7,475 to 17,032 bytes and gained webextension-polyfill when the flag was passed), and `extension dev` applies it by default already. Fixed 2026-09-09, one finding corrected and one withdrawn as a false positive. Step 6 now carries the corrected polyfill rule, identical in substance to the from-crxjs page and backed by the same measurements on 4.1.15. The `plasmo package` finding does not hold and the page is left as written. plasmo 0.90.5 lists `package` on the CMDS line of its help output (help, start, init, dev, build, package, version, -v, --version), its dist/index.js command map has a `package` entry alongside dev and build, and `npx plasmo@0.90.5 package` in a scratch project reaches the command and logs `Prepare to package the extension bundle...` before failing on a missing tsconfig.json. Only the per-command OPTS block of that help output is limited to init, dev and build, which is the part the original check appears to have read. So the page's `plasmo dev` / `plasmo build` / `plasmo package` mapping onto `extension dev` / `extension build --zip` stands. One prose semicolon was also removed.

Four findings, all substantive rather than cosmetic. First, the conclusion is inverted. The English page opens its Vite 8 section with `Mostly historical` and states that on current versions the error does not reproduce in common setups, while the Chinese page says Vite 8's defaults turned the error from an edge case into a common one. Second, the recommended fix order is inverted. The Chinese page makes pinning `vite@^7 --save-exact` its first remedy and describes upgrading the plugin as a project that is still gradually adding Rolldown compatibility, which stopped being true when crxjs/chrome-extension-tools#1132 closed. Third, the version guidance is missing entirely: `@crxjs/vite-plugin@2.7.0` appears nowhere in the translation, and neither do the #1042, #1067 and #1132 references that carry the evidence, leaving only #883. Fourth, the page carries two sections with no English counterpart, a structural-fix pitch containing an extra `npx extension@latest dev` fence and a See also list, which is where the extra `dev` command, the `--save-exact` flag and the four extra internal links reported by the parity comparison come from.
